note: A full run is interactive (AskUserQuestion rounds) and its depth depends on the specific unknowns present, so this eval checks policy comprehension of the skill text directly rather than a full run.

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text only: (1) The request is to fix an off-by-one error in a function the user has touched a dozen times before, in a part of the codebase they know well. What should discover do? (2) Can more than one mode run in a single invocation, and if so, in what order? (3) What is the interview mode's questioning cadence, and why is it shaped that way? (4) For UI-affecting brainstorm/prototype work, what gets built, and which skill is recommended (not invoked) for the mockups' construction quality? (5) What two files does discover produce, and why does it write both an HTML artifact and a plain-markdown companion instead of just one?
assertions: Answer 1: say so plainly and recommend /to-plan directly - no mode should run just to look thorough when no real unknown is present

Answer 2: yes, more than one mode can run in one invocation, in whatever sequence the situation needs (e.g. blind spot pass surfacing a shape decision that brainstorm/prototype explores, which then surfaces ambiguities the interview resolves) - never a fixed pipeline

Answer 3: one question at a time, ordered by architectural impact rather than batched - because each answer can retire or reshape the next question, so batching would waste rounds on now-irrelevant questions
Answer 4: 2-4 cheap HTML mockups of wildly different directions with fake data; artifact-design is recommended for construction quality, not invoked
Answer 5: a published HTML discovery artifact and a plain-markdown {topic-slug}-discovery-notes.md companion - the markdown companion is what to-plan reads back in directly without parsing HTML
